we have solved two crystal structures of K. pneumoniae carbapenem-hydrolyzing β-lactamases, one with a small molecule boronic acid and the other with a penam sulfone, both of which are β-lactam inhibitors that follow different inhibition mechanisms and kinetics.

the development of a new class of boronic acid-based inhibitors of KPC- 2 β-lactamases.
the development of novel β-lactam inhibitors for the treatment of infections due to multidrug-resistant Gram-negative pathogens.
the structure and function of KPC-1 and KPC-2 carbapenem hydrolyzing β-lactamases, and the design of novel inhibitors.

the crystallographic data and the biochemical data are consistent with the hypothesis that the two inhibitors bind and inhibit in different ways.
